name: Apollo 11 // Mare Tranquillitatis
targetDescription: West Crater boulder field sample rim
historicalNotes: First crewed lunar landing by Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on July 20, 1969. Armstrong manually steered past a football-field-sized boulder field with ~25 seconds of fuel remaining.

name: Apollo 12 // Oceanus Procellarum
historicalNotes: Pinpoint touchdown within 160 meters of the robotic Surveyor 3 lander, demonstrating precision lunar guidance.

name: Apollo 15 // Hadley-Apennine
targetDescription: Hadley Rille basaltic lava gorge rim
historicalNotes: First 'J-mission' featuring the Lunar Roving Vehicle near the 4,000-meter peaks of the Apennine Mountains.

name: Apollo 17 // Taurus-Littrow Valley
targetDescription: Shorty Crater orange pyroclastic soil deposit
historicalNotes: Final Apollo landing conducted by Eugene Cernan and geologist Harrison Schmitt in a deep mountain-flanked valley.

name: Chandrayaan-3 // Shiv Shakti Point
historicalNotes: ISRO's historic August 2023 soft landing, making India the first nation to touch down in the lunar southern polar highlands.

name: Chang'e 4 // Von Kármán Crater (Farside)
historicalNotes: First soft landing on the lunar far side in January 2019, communicating via the Queqiao relay satellite at Earth-Moon L2.

name: Artemis III // Shackleton Connecting Ridge
targetDescription: Permanently shadowed crater volatile ice trap
historicalNotes: Artemis polar exploration candidate featuring peaks of eternal light adjacent to sub-surface cryogenic ice reserves.

name: Perseverance // Jezero Crater Delta
historicalNotes: Mars 2020 entry, descent, and landing using Range Trigger and Terrain-Relative Navigation to land directly beside ancient river channels.
